description:
norvel v5 (direction: music, rhythm and dance) - A DRUM GRID: THE SNARE HIT NOBODY IS HOLDING
SKIDS LATE. PRIVATE; never shown to players. Earlier versions: norvel.v1..v4.json.

WHY v5. v4 is calibrated ON RATE (6 Opus finals: 100/100/100 % with a demo, 15/14/14 % without)
but the judge scores the kid test 3.67: "the grid's width and glyph vocabulary ask a lot of visual
bookkeeping before the which-row question even opens up; shrink to the minimum bar count that
still plants all four near-misses, and rename the caption '<n> snare slip' so a demo-less reader
is nudged toward the snare row without the count giving away which hits move". v5 is a
SALIENCE-ONLY pass: the rule, the plants, the ~12 % n = 0 foothold and the witness profile are
byte-for-byte the v4 design; only the drawing changed.

CLUE = A FINISHED DRUM GRID, four lines (seed 227):

      hat |..xx|..xx|x..x|..xx|.x.x|
    snare |.x..|.x.x|.x..|..x.|x.x.|
     kick |..x.|.xx.|..x.|x...|x...|
    3 snare slip

SOLUTION = the same picture with the snare row edited:

      hat |..xx|..xx|x..x|..xx|.x.x|
    snare |.-x.|.x.x|.--x|..x.|x.-x|
     kick |..x.|.xx.|..x.|x...|x...|
    3 snare slip

THE RULE (one clause, UNCHANGED from v4). A snare hit with NO HAT ABOVE IT AND NO KICK UNDER IT -
a step where the snare is left playing on its own - skids late: it is drawn "-" where it stood,
"-" on across the hat's gap, and lands "x" on the first step where the hat is ticking again.
Nothing else changes. Kid sentence from one demo: "when the hat stops ticking and the kick isn't
there either, the snare hit has nothing to hold it, so it skids along until the hat catches it."
In the demo above the hit in bar 1 skids one step, the hit in bar 3 skids two (the hat is off
over both steps and back on the fourth), and the second hit of bar 5 skids one; the first hits of
bars 2 and 5 sit under a hat hole too but a kick is under them, so they stay put; the second hit
of bar 2 and the hit of bar 4 have the hat above them. Four kinds of near-miss, one demo.

WHAT CHANGED IN v5 (drawing only)
1. THE GRID IS THE SMALLEST ONE THAT STILL CARRIES EVERY PLANT. Measured per n over 3000 clues:
   the mandatory hat holes are n (skid origins) + 1 (the two-step skid) + 2 (over kicked snare
   hits) + 1 (over a lone kick) + 2 (over empty steps), and at most 2 holes may fall in one bar,
   so the floor is 4 bars for n <= 1, 5 bars for n = 2-3 and 6 bars for n = 4. Below that the
   generator cannot place the plants at all: at 4 bars every n >= 2 clue fails 300/300 attempts,
   at 5 bars every n = 4 clue does (10 holes into 10 slots of capacity). 3 bars IS placeable for
   n <= 1, but 12 steps is too small a canvas to be worth it: only 70 % of the n = 1 clues are
   then distinct (one picture recurs 15 times in 60 000 seeds) against 100 % at 4 bars, and the
   offline elimination the caption pays for needs ~30 DIFFERENT harvested clues. v5 ships the
   smallest grid that keeps the clue space intact, B = (4,4,5,5,6)[n]: 4.97 bars mean against v4's 7.07, 60 cells to read against 84,
   a clue line of 27/32/37 chars against 37/42/47. The snare and kick counts are scaled with the grid
   (m = B..B+3 hits, B-2..B+1 free kicks) so the shrunk grid reads as the same groove and not as
   a denser one: snare 33 % -> 37 % of the steps, kick 35 % -> 36 %. The one density that really
   rises is the hat's holes, 32 % -> 43 %, and that is forced - the plants need the same 6-11
   holes and there are 29 % fewer steps to put them in.
2. THE CAPTION NAMES THE ROW: "3 snare slip" instead of "3 slip". It does not say WHICH hits move
   or how many hat holes there are, so it is still exactly the v4 checksum. The scorer ignores
   any line with no x/./- in it, so the answer may keep this caption, keep the OLD "3 slip"
   caption, reword it, move it or drop it entirely - all score identically (house rule 2026-09-05,
   verified at 100 % on 1000 clues for each variant).
3. THE ROWS ARE RIGHT-ALIGNED ONTO THE STAFF ("  hat |", "snare |", " kick |") so the bar lines
   form one clean left edge. REJECTED: "hi-hat" as a label - "-" is a glyph the scorer compares,
   so a dash in a label would corrupt the row it labels; a fancier bar line (":", "||") - solve
   and score walk the grid by skipping "|", so any other separator would need the scorer and the
   whole witness table rebuilt for no legibility gain; drawing rests as "-" (real drum tab) -
   "-" is the ghost glyph, so rests stay "." and the contrast tick/silence/ghost is x / . / -.
4. EXACTLY ONE TWO-STEP SKID per clue when n >= 2 (v4: at least one, sometimes two or three).
   The demo still contradicts "it moves one step later" from inside one picture, but the answer
   carries fewer dash runs.
5. THE SKIDDING HITS ARE PICKED FOR A READABLE LANDING where the grid allows it (the two steps
   after the hit are free and no other skid is within four steps; a second pass takes anything if
   that fails). Demos in which every skid's origin and landing read as separate marks: 13 % -> 37 %
   (per skid 40 % -> 62 %). This is the one change with a measurable side effect: see the leak
   note below.

CONSTRUCTION (generate). B as above; m = B..B+3 snare hits (>= n+4), never two adjacent and never
on the last step; 2-4 of them over a kick; B-2..B+1 further kicks; at least two snare hits left
over with the hat ticking above them; the hat plays every step except the holes, at most 2 per
bar. n is drawn 0(12 %)/1(10 %)/2(29 %)/3(29 %)/4(20 %) BEFORE any retry, so the distribution is
exact. Every clue plants the near-misses that make one demo enough:
  * >= 2 snare hits with the hat still ticking and no kick under them (they stay)
  * >= 2 snare hits under a hat hole but with a kick under them      (they stay)
  * >= 1 hat hole over a kick alone and >= 2 over empty steps        (nothing happens)
  * n >= 2: one skid of one step and one of two steps; one skid lands on a kick and one lands on
    an empty step (so "it only skids when the way is clear" and its mirror die on the caption)
and n is refused whenever it equals a count a player could read straight off the picture (snare
hits, kicks, hat holes, snare hits over a kick, snare hits with no hat, kicks with no hat, holes
with no snare, bars, ...) so the caption cannot be explained by anything but the rule. All 3000
sampled clues carry all four near-miss kinds and both skid lengths; 0 fallbacks in 50 000 seeds.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (a) from the clue alone: a drum grid, the answer is this picture with
the snare row edited - and v5's caption says which row - so a demo-less player echoes the clue and
banks the 12 % of clues that say "0 snare slip"; (b) harvest ~30 clues and find the one predicate
whose count is always the caption: the snare hits standing alone in their column; (c) the demo
shows what an edit looks like: a dash where the hit stood, dashes across the hat's gap, the hit
landing on the next hat tick; (d) both skid lengths are in the same picture, so the "until the hat
catches it" reading is forced rather than "one step later".

WITNESS TABLE (3000 fresh clues, the v4 attacks, v4 -> v5)
  the true rule (solve)                                            100.00 -> 100.00 %
  clue echoed unchanged (the foothold: the "0 snare slip" clues)    11.70 ->  11.70 %
  RIGHT RULE, WRONG DRAWING (a player without the demo):
    hit moves one step later, no ghost                              11.70 ->  11.70 %
    ghost + hit one step later                                      21.23 ->  21.23 %
    hit stays, a copy one step later / glyph change in place        11.70 ->  11.70 %
    moves past the hat's gap without ghosts / stays + copy past it  11.70 ->  11.70 %
    ghosts but skidding EARLIER                                     11.70 ->  11.70 %
  WRONG RULE, RIGHT DRAWING (a player with the demo):
    every snare hit with no hat above it                             0.00 ->   0.00 %
    every snare hit with no kick under it                            0.00 ->   0.00 %
    every snare hit over a kick / every snare hit                     0.00 ->   0.00 %
    the same rule applied to the kick row                            0.00 ->   0.00 %
    the n leftmost snare hits                                       13.10 ->  12.77 %
    n random snare hits chosen from those with no hat above         24.40 ->  24.50 %
    lone hits but only when no kick lands on the landing step       31.60 ->  31.73 %
    lone hits but only when the hat is off on the next step too     11.70 ->  11.70 %
  demo replay / empty / junk / unicode / 4000 chars / snare row alone /
    rows swapped / the snare row shifted one step                    0.00 ->   0.00 %
  leniency (all 100 %): bare rows with no bars and no labels, other labels, a "|1234|"
    beat header, blank lines, CRLF, tabs, prose around the picture, spaces around the
    bar lines, the caption kept / dropped / reworded / replaced by v4's "n slip"
  strictness (all 0 %): rows swapped, two rows, four rows, one row, the snare row shifted,
    ghosts turned into rests, ghosts turned into hits, all on one line, one wrong hat cell
Gradient unchanged: 0 % (well-formed but the wrong hits) -> 12 % (the format and the "0" clues)
-> 21-32 % (the right hits, the drawing or a spurious extra condition wrong) -> 100 %.

THE ONE MEASURED SIDE EFFECT of the readable-landing preference (change 5): rivals that pick the
skidding hits by the GAP AFTER THEM instead of by lone-ness gain a few points - "the n hits with
the biggest gap after them" 14.5 % (v4) -> 17.4 % (v5 geometry alone) -> 20.3 % (with the
preference), "every hit with >= 2 free steps after it" 7.2 -> 12.8 %. They stay below the 24.5 %
of the best half-insight rival and below the 25 % bar, and a player who reaches them still has to
find the drawing; the trade bought three times as many readable demos. If a player ever plateaus
at ~20 %, drop the preference (the two lines marked "prefer a landing that reads clearly").

VALIDATION. quickcheck --seeds 200: OK, one warning ("score accepts the clue itself as a
solution") which is the intended n = 0 foothold and is raised identically by kelmar, fennick and
durnel. score 312/512 (UNCHANGED from v4 - the caption never
reaches the comparison), solve 472/5000, generate 5303/50000; clue <= 126 chars (v4: 150),
solution <= 126. generate
deterministic, 0.34 ms mean over 20 000 seeds (p99 1.8 ms, max 3.4 ms, 0 fallbacks in 50 000);
solve 0.003 ms and scores 1 on 3000/3000 fresh clues; score 0.020 ms (worst 0.43 ms on junk).
Scorer: 0 raises, 0 non-binary results and 0 false positives on 12 000 junk strings; 0
disagreements with an independent re-implementation on 12 000 mutated answers.

LEVERS. Too easy (a player cracks it without a demo): drop the ghost dashes across the gap so the
drawing is a single "-" and an "x"; make the hat hole above a skidding hit sometimes three steps
wide; stop printing the caption on 1 clue in 4. Too hard (a demo-holder stays under 30 %): let the
skid always be one step; guarantee two lone hits in the same bar; put two worked skids in a
picture with only five snare hits.
generate:
# THE PICTURE: three drum rows over B bars of four steps (hat on top, then snare, then
# kick) and a caption "<n> snare slip".  THE RULE (one clause): a snare hit with no hat
# above it and no kick under it -- a step where the snare is left playing on its own --
# skids late: it is drawn "-" where it stood, "-" on across the hat's gap, and lands "x"
# on the first step where the hat is ticking again.  n counts the skidding hits and is 0
# in ~12 % of clues, where the echoed clue scores.
# B is the SMALLEST bar count that still carries every plant for that n (4/4/5/5/6 for
# n = 0..4); the snare and kick counts are scaled with it (snare 37 % of the steps, kick
# 36 %, against v4's 33 / 35) so the shrunk grid reads as the same groove, not a denser
# one.  3 bars is placeable for n <= 1 but collapses the clue space (70 % distinct).
# Every clue plants the near-misses that make ONE demo enough:
#   * >= 2 snare hits with the hat still ticking and no kick under (stay put)
#   * >= 2 snare hits under a hat hole but with a kick under them (they stay)
#   * >= 1 hat hole over a kick alone, >= 2 over empty steps       (nothing happens)
#   * when n >= 2, ONE skid of two steps and ONE of a single step, so no constant
#     distance renders the answer and the demo shows the hat catching the hit
#   * when n >= 2, one skid lands on a kick and one lands on an empty step
FB = ("  hat |x.xx|.x.x|x.x.|xx.x|x..x|\n"
      "snare |x.x.|x.x.|...x|.x.x|.x..|\n"
      " kick |x..x|x.xx|xx..|x...|....|\n"
      "2 snare slip")


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    n = 0 if r.random() < 0.12 else r.choice((1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4))
    for _ in range(300):
        B = (4, 4, 5, 5, 6)[n]                           # the smallest grid that fits
        L = 4 * B
        m = r.randint(max(B, n + 4), B + 3)              # snare hits, never adjacent
        S = sorted(r.sample(range(L - m), m))
        S = [p + i for i, p in enumerate(S)]             # gaps >= 2, last step free
        Ss = set(S)
        uu = [v for v in range(2, min(4, m - n - 2) + 1) if v != n]
        if not uu:
            continue
        both = r.sample(S, r.choice(uu))                 # snare hits over a kick
        rest = [i for i in range(L) if i not in Ss and i != L - 1]
        K = set(both) | set(r.sample(rest, r.randint(B - 2, B + 1)))
        cand = [i for i in S if i not in K]              # could be left playing alone
        if len(cand) < n + 2:                            # >= 2 stay put under the hat
            continue
        r.shuffle(cand); r.shuffle(both); r.shuffle(rest)
        cnt = [0] * B                                    # hat holes per bar: at most 2
        A = []
        for w in (1, 0):                                 # the hits that skid: prefer
            for a in cand:                               # a landing that reads clearly
                if len(A) < n and not cnt[a // 4] and (
                        not w or (a + 2 not in Ss and a + 3 not in Ss
                                  and all(abs(a - b) > 4 for b in A))):
                    A.append(a)
                    cnt[a // 4] = 1
        if len(A) < n:
            continue
        # a two-step skid: the hat is missing over the next step as well.  With n >= 2
        # the clue always shows one skid of each length.
        el = [a for a in A if a + 2 not in Ss and a + 2 < L and cnt[(a + 1) // 4] < 2]
        if n > 1 and not el:
            continue
        ext = set()
        if n > 1:                                        # exactly one two-step skid
            ext.add(el[0] + 1)
            cnt[(el[0] + 1) // 4] += 1
        keep = {a + 1 for a in A} | {a + 2 for a in A}   # the hat must come back here
        holes = set(A) | ext
        free = [i for i in rest if i not in keep]

        def add(pool, k):
            got = 0
            for i in pool:
                if got < k and cnt[i // 4] < 2:
                    holes.add(i)
                    cnt[i // 4] += 1
                    got += 1
            return got

        if not (add([i for i in both if i not in keep], 2) > 1  # over kicked snare hits
                and add([i for i in free if i in K], 1)         # over a kick on its own
                and add([i for i in free if i not in K], 2 + (r.random() < .5)) > 1):
            continue
        land = [a + 2 if a + 1 in ext else a + 1 for a in A]
        if n > 1 and len({j in K for j in land}) < 2:
            continue                                     # one lands on a kick, one free
        # counts a player could read off the picture instead of finding the rule
        if n and n in (m, len(K), len(holes), len(both), len(cand), B, len(ext),
                       len([i for i in S if i in holes]),
                       len([i for i in K if i in holes]),
                       len([i for i in holes if i not in Ss]),
                       len([i for i in S if i not in holes and i not in K])):
            continue
        row = lambda p: "|" + "|".join(
            "".join("x" if 4 * b + j in p else "." for j in range(4))
            for b in range(B)) + "|"
        return ("  hat " + row(set(range(L)) - holes) + "\n" + "snare " + row(Ss)
                + "\n" + " kick " + row(K) + "\n" + str(n) + " snare slip")
    return FB
solve:
def solve(clue):
    H, S, K, T = clue.split("\n")
    E = list(S)
    for i, q in enumerate(S):
        if q == "x" and H[i] == "." and K[i] == ".":
            j = i
            E[i] = "-"
            while H[j] == ".":                # skid on across the hat's gap
                j += 1 + (S[j + 1] == "|")
                E[j] = "-"
            E[j] = "x"                        # land where the hat ticks again
    return H + "\n" + "".join(E) + "\n" + K + "\n" + T
